Astra continuation, 2026-10-31

MAIN CHOICE

The strongest opening developed here is a way to qualify operations against a
large, disordered quantum source without bounding its entire many-body energy
band. The quantity that matters for finite-time energy isolation is the
source's ability to CHANGE THE COUPLING, measured by a local commutator. An
explicit cycle uses fresh lower-state orbital carriers to remove energy from
spin-selective charge transfer. It replaces repeated complete charge tests by
unobserved, spin-blind energy-removal contacts and two final charge tests.

The general isolation estimate and the finite-contact cycle are proved below.
The Coulomb matrix element and all accompanying projected terms are derived in
the companion physical-contact note. A screened source supplies a concrete
large-source domain. These results are not a demonstrated semiconductor device
window, a new universal-computation theorem, or a fault-tolerance threshold.
Repeated-interaction cooling, capacitive quantum-dot control, and spin blockade
are established mechanisms. The contribution is their source-uniform complete
operation and the admission criterion, with the actual resources exposed.

1. Why a whole-source bandwidth is the wrong default

A bare orbital or charge gap is insufficient: a source transition can resonantly
bridge it. The earlier split-manifold and orbital counterexamples remain valid.
But the sufficient condition 'gap exceeds the ENTIRE source spectrum' is often
far too strong. A source of N local cells has an extensive spectrum even when a
particular local operator can transfer only a small amount of energy efficiently.

There are two complementary formulations. The first is an exact finite-time
unitary estimate; it does not use a master equation, a secular approximation,
an initial source state, or any minimum source level spacing. The second is a
spectral sum rule useful for passive reservoirs. The first is the operative
admission proof for the cold-carrier construction here.

31 October 2026. Analytic proof and independent numerical checks.

Verdict
-------
The proposed bound is correct. It controls the complete unitary, not only
populations, and needs neither a source spectral gap nor the norm or total

give small error when a noncommuting resonant source can supply the bare
orbital energy. The extension to time-dependent common source evolution is
valid with a fixed dressing generator and an integral of the commutator
bound. No source-Hamiltonian derivative is required.

Work first in finite dimension, with an arbitrary reference system implicitly
tensored throughout. Let

 H = H_c + I_carrier tensor H_E + W + V,
 H_ref = H_c + I_carrier tensor H_E + W.

Here H_c is source-independent and self-adjoint. Write its carrier spectral
resolution H_c=sum_a E_a P_a, allowing degeneracies. Let V=V^dagger have no
matrix elements between equal-energy sectors; those elements belong in W.
Define

 S_ab = V_ab/(E_a-E_b),  E_a!=E_b,

PHYSICAL VALVE, PASSIVE OUTLET, AND A SCREENED ACTIVE SOURCE
31 October 2026. Complementary calculation for the Astra continuation.

Scope
-----
This note earns an additive, spin-independent resonator coupling from an
electrostatic projection; identifies the exact singlet capture/return chain;
gives a bounded full-mode spectral admission construction; and supplies an
extensive-source domain in which local energy-transfer estimates can replace
a total source bandwidth. These are distinct levels of assertion.

The finite admitted valve is exact. The static system block reduction has
explicit bounds. A cold, passive, broad reservoir has a controlled limiting
description, but no numerical finite-band, full-record approximation error is
proved here. The numerical examples certify the specified matrices, not an
interacting semiconductor device. The inherited loading, source, S/T return,
triplet preservation, and charge-dark-state corrections remain in force.

Later same-session development: LOCAL_ADMISSION_AUDIT.txt proves a stronger
FINITE-TIME route using ||[H_E,V]|| rather than a total source bandwidth.
Consequently the global-band construction in section 4 is one sufficient
method, not a necessary source-resource condition. The new bound also keeps
complete unitary/instrument errors. Applying it to an unbounded oscillator
still requires its stated bounded-interaction/domain hypotheses; the finite
two-level carrier construction avoids that issue directly.

1. Microscopic electrostatic projection: additive is the earned coupling
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Let w_L,w_R be real orthonormal localized orbitals, with w_R(x)=w_L(-x).
A cavity/barrier-mode electrostatic potential is u(x)(a+a^dagger), with real
even u. Its exact projection on those orbitals is

 H_cav = (a+a^dagger)[d(n_L+n_R)+g_c K],
 K=sum_sigma(c_Lsigma^dagger c_Rsigma+c_Rsigma^dagger c_Lsigma),
 d=int |w_L|^2 u=int |w_R|^2 u,
 g_c=int w_L w_R u (real).

At fixed data number n_L+n_R=2 the diagonal term is a COMMON SCALAR force.
With b=a+2d/omega,

 omega a^dagger a+2d(a+a^dagger)+g_c K(a+a^dagger)
 =omega b^dagger b+g_c K(b+b^dagger)-(4d g_c/omega)K+constant.

Thus the common force is removed exactly by a known displacement, and the
static hopping acquires a known scalar correction. The mode to cool is b.
This does not require a source-dependent displacement.
